voice: Ship AI (the narrator): warm, clear, encouraging mission-control voice; British or Indian English; age 25-35; smiling; never rushed.

lines.text: Welcome, Space Commander! We have a new landing mission.
Our landing site is on that ocean planet.
Use the joystick to turn the ship. Put the planet inside the circle.
Locked on! Now push the thrust lever all the way up.
Wow! A planet covered in water.
Hold the DESCEND button to fly down through the clouds.
We need to find a safe place for it to land.
Let's send the survey drone to check the area.
Click the LAUNCH button to launch the drone.
It is too dark to see the landing zones.
Start the scanner to search the area.
Great! The scanner found five landing zones.
Look! Each landing zone has a different shape.
Five spaceships are on their way to this planet, and each one has a different shape.
Each spaceship must land on the zone that matches it perfectly, not too small and not too big.
To find the perfect spot for every spaceship, we need to know the area of these shapes.
So let's learn how to find the area of each shape!
Hello, Commander! Let's learn about area together.
The area of a shape is the amount of space it covers.
We measure area in square units. Each small square is one square unit.
This square has sides of 4 units.
Let's fill it with unit squares: 4 rows, with 4 squares in each row.
That makes 16 square units. 4 times 4 is 16.
So, the area of a square is side times side.
Your turn! A square has sides of 6 units. What is its area?
24 is the distance all the way around the square. Area is the space inside it.
12 is 6 plus 6. For area, multiply side times side.
Side times side is 6 times 6, which is 36.
This rectangle is 5 units long and 3 units wide.
It has 3 rows, with 5 unit squares in each row.
5 times 3 is 15. So its area is 15 square units.
The area of a rectangle is length times width.
A rectangle is 7 units long and 4 units wide. What is its area?
22 is the distance all the way around the rectangle. For area, multiply length times width.
11 is 7 plus 4. For area, multiply length times width.
Length times width is 7 times 4, which is 28.
Here is a parallelogram. Its base is 6 units, and its height is 4 units.
The height goes straight up from the base, at a right angle. It is not the slanted side.
Watch! Cut off this triangle, and move it to the other side.
Now it is a rectangle, 6 units long and 4 units wide. 6 times 4 is 24 square units.
So, the area of a parallelogram is base times height.
A parallelogram has a base of 9 units, a height of 4 units, and a slanted side of 5 units. What is its area?
45 uses the slanted side. Use the height, which makes a right angle with the base.
28 is the distance all the way around it. For area, multiply base times height.
Base times height is 9 times 4, which is 36.
This is a rhombus. All four of its sides are the same length.
Its diagonals are 10 units and 4 units long. They cross at a right angle.
Let's draw a rectangle around it, 10 units long and 4 units wide.
Look! The four corner pieces fit exactly onto the rhombus. So the rhombus is half of the rectangle.
Half of 10 times 4 is 20 square units.
So, the area of a rhombus is half times diagonal 1 times diagonal 2.
A rhombus has diagonals of 12 units and 5 units. What is its area?
60 is the whole rectangle around the rhombus. Don't forget to take half!
17 is 12 plus 5. Multiply the diagonals, then take half.
Half of 12 times 5 is half of 60, which is 30.
This is a trapezium. Its two parallel sides are 3 units and 7 units, and its height is 4 units.
Let's make a copy, and turn it upside down.
Put the two together, and they make a parallelogram!
Its base is 3 plus 7, which is 10 units, and its height is 4 units. So its area is 10 times 4, which is 40.
One trapezium is half of that: 20 square units.
So, the area of a trapezium is half times the sum of the parallel sides times the height.
A trapezium has parallel sides of 5 units and 9 units, and a height of 4 units. What is its area?
56 is the whole parallelogram. One trapezium is only half of it!
36 uses only one of the parallel sides. Add both parallel sides first.
5 plus 9 is 14. Half of 14 times 4 is 28.
That's right! Well done.
Correct! Excellent work.
Spot on, Commander!
Brilliant! You've got it.
Perfect! That's the area.
Not quite. Try again!
Now choose the glowing answer.
Welcome back, Space Commander! Now you know how to find the area of every shape.
Let's land the spaceships, one by one.
Here comes our first spaceship!
Next, we need to find how much space the spaceship needs.
Its area is side times side.
Calculate the area of the spaceship, and select the land with the required area.
Here comes our second spaceship!
Its area is length times width.
Find the area of the spaceship, and select the suitable land.
Great landings, Commander! Three more spaceships are waiting. Let's bring them down!
Here comes our third spaceship!
Its area is base times height.
Here comes our fourth spaceship!
Its area is half times diagonal 1 times diagonal 2.
Here comes our last spaceship!
Its area is half times the sum of the parallel sides times the height.
Perfect match! The spaceship fits exactly.
Landing successful! Great work, Space Commander.
This landing zone is too small. The spaceship cannot fit safely.
This landing zone is too large. Try to find the exact match.
Choose the landing zone with the exact area.
Out of hearts! Autopilot will land on the zone that fits.

Work out side times side: 5 times 5.
24 is the distance all the way around the ship. For area, multiply length times width.
Check the width: it is 4 units. Length times width is 8 times 4.
26 is the distance all the way around the ship. Area is base times height.
42 uses the slanted side. Use the height: base times height.
20 is the distance all the way around the ship. Area is half of diagonal 1 times diagonal 2.
Multiply the two diagonals, then take half.
40 uses only the shorter parallel side. Add both parallel sides first.
60 uses only the longer parallel side. Add both parallel sides first.
Here's a hint. Work out 5 times 5.
Here's a hint. Work out 8 times 4.
Here's a hint. Work out 7 times 5.
Here's a hint. Work out half of 6 times 8.
Here's a hint. Add 8 and 12, then multiply by 5, and take half.
All five spaceships have landed safely. Great work, Space Commander!
